column2: The oldest game here: a missed king shot, then a comeback turn.
The world championship on Gotland, scored from video with no player names.
On snow. The scorer says which turns were guessed before the video starts.
A missed king shot that would have won the tournament, then a six-kubb drill.
The richest record: 20 turns, a note on most, video and the paper scoresheet.
The 2012 US Nationals final, with punishment kubbs and where they were placed.
The shortest game: the king falls in turn 3.
The biggest comeback: five base kubbs behind, plus an illegal throw and a king miss.
On a frozen lake: a winning drill in five turns.
A Belgian final won from three base kubbs behind in four turns.
Two king shots thrown between the legs miss, then the next one lands.
The Canadian final: two missed king shots before the win.
The longest game: 23 turns, one against one, and a forgotten advantage line.
The 2-4-6 opening: two batons, then four, then six.
